resolved.title: 从FOR循环开始
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Loops[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Loops can execute a block of code a number of times. They’re handy when you want to run the same code repeatedly, adding a different value each time.

JavaScript has three types of loops: [b]for[/b], [b]while[/b], and [b]do while[/b]. 

We’ll start here with the classic [b]for [/b]loop.

[s0l0!-header][b]Here's the syntax:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="js" ]for (statement 1; statement 2; statement 3) {
   code block to be executed
}[/code]
[i][/i][b][/b]And here’s what happens when it runs:

[b]Statement 1[/b] is executed before the loop (the code block) starts.
[b]Statement 2[/b] defines the condition for running the loop (the code block).
[b]Statement 3[/b] is executed each time after the loop (the code block) has been executed.
[note][b]Heads up![/b]
As you can see, the [b]classic for loop[/b] has [b]three [/b]components, or statements.[/note]

[s0l0!-header][h1]The for loop[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

"Repetition is the mother of learning, the father of action, which makes it the architect of accomplishment." - Zig Ziglar.
Inspired by these words, let's create a little program that will output an expression which is given as input, 3 times.

[b]Task[/b]
Complete the code to output the given expression 3 times.

[b]Sample Input[/b]
Learning is fun!

[b]Sample Output[/b]
Learning is fun!
Learning is fun!
Learning is fun!

[note]Use the [b]for loop[/b] to run the required part of the code as many times as needed.[/note]
